name_reason: Follows fd2_<domain>_<descriptor>. The '30' is the chapter number (chapters 01-30 are valid domain IDs), confirmed by the body calling fd2_load_chapter_battle_data(0x1E) where 0x1E==30; it is NOT address residue (the function's own address is 0x2C405). The descriptor accurately reflects behavior: plays the chapter-30 final per-character portrait + epilogue monologue sequence in the endgame.
purpose: Chapter-30 endgame sequence: opening text + palette breathing sweep, then for each menu-party member (reverse order) plays an intro zoom, figani pose animation, and an RNG-driven mouth-jittered portrait/epilogue monologue, fading to black between characters.
logic_summary: __CHK(0x5C). Loads chapter-30 battle data (idx 0x1E); sets dialog portrait blit offset to 0xC88. Allocates 0x36B00 workspace, renders chapter-30 opening text (page 0x2C), runs a 500-frame palette breathing sweep (brightness 0x28 fades to 0 over frames <200, fades back up after frame 300), frees workspace. Reallocates a 0x1F400 workspace + two 64000-byte buffers (bg_buf, scratch); loads TAI.DAT[3] backdrop sprite and FDOTHER.DAT[0x38] RLE base image into bg_buf; starts ending BGM track 4. Reverse-iterates the menu party (count-1 down to 0) with a 0/1 display-slot swap (char_idx 0->slot 1, char_idx 1->slot 0) so the two leads trade order; per member: portrait_id = runtime_char[swap_idx].portrait_id, figani_idx = portrait_id*3; loads FIGANI.DAT pose_data (figani_idx+1) and sprite_sheet (figani_idx); plays the intro zoom then a 20-tick pose hold; walks the pose-step table (count=pose_data[2], step_offset read as int32 at pose_data+s*4+8, per-step delay=pose_data[step_offset+6]); snapshots bg_buf->scratch, loads DATO.DAT[portrait_id] portrait, frames the dialog panel; the last member (char_idx 0) gets a 0x1B8-tick monologue, others 0xDC. Per tick: render frame; RNG-driven mouth jitter (counter reload = (advance_rng()&0x1F)+0x28, frame_offset 0xC when counter<2 else 0); blit portrait via *(int*)(portrait_buf+frame_offset); step figani; assemble 5 dialog fragments (header page 10, char name all_game_text[char_id+1], separator page 0xB, job name all_game_text[job_id+0x96], and epilogue page = char_id+0xC for t<0xDC else 0x2D closer); flip to screen; a key press sets char_idx=1 to break out and clears the buffer. Fade to black between members. Frees bg_buf/scratch/pose_data/bg_sprite/workspace (final free is a tail jump into the free-wrapper epilogue).
comment_original_issue: Comment content was accurate and precise, but contained 6 non-ASCII em-dash characters (U+2014) in the EAX-bug note and Resources list, violating the src/tests ASCII-only rule. Converted each to '--'. No semantic change.
notes: EAX-tracking-bug correctly reproduced in src: machine code at 0x2C99C does CALL fd2_advance_rng_state; AND AL,0x1F; ADD AL,0x28 (jitter from RNG return, not the DATO buffer); decompiler mis-renders it as (byte)DATO_load_result&0x1F. Source line 863 reads pose step_offset as int32 at pose_data+s*4+8 and line 870 delay as pose_data[step_offset+6], both confirmed against asm 0x2C6FD-0x2C76F. Ghidra plate uses the decompiler's undefined4* rendering (pose_data[s+2] / [step_offset+6]) which is byte-equivalent to the src's byte-pointer rendering -- no contradiction, plate left untouched. The two filename string globals carry address-residue suffixes (_52388, _51a70) but those are data symbols out of scope for this function refine. Param list empty (void). Sole caller fd2_play_game_ending_cinematic @ 0x2BCE5 (call site 0x2C18F).
